title: New recommendations after death in custody
article: Four years after Christopher Hiebert died in police custody, the province is making new recommendations regarding the care of prisoners.
A public inquest into the death of Hiebert was held in Saskatoon last week. In its findings, the coroner's jury said paramedics should be present at all times in the detention centre.
Other recommendations include more first aid training for detention workers and a consent form to allow access to a prisoner's medical records.
Hiebert, 34, was arrested Sept. 9 for outstanding fraud and theft charges. He was found in his cell in medical distress shortly after his arrest. He was taken to hospital where he later died.
Hiebert's mother, Lee, said she called at least three times between 11:15 p.m. CST and midnight, but she never heard back about whether officers were checking on her son.
